mainTopic: Sources for the communal offering, the role of one tribe according to רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון, why one tribe counts as a קהל, and the חטאת of the לוים
overview: The גמרא first finds the source for רבי מאיר and רבי שמעון's rule that the ruling comes from the בית דין and the action from the people. אביי and רבא each bring a פסוק, and both פסוקים turn out to be needed. A גזרה שוה of the word מעיני carries the rule from עבודה זרה to all sins. Next the גמרא asks, in רבי יהודה's view, whether the other tribes bring offerings when one tribe sinned by a ruling of the בית דין הגדול. After one proof is pushed away, a ברייתא and the wording of the משנה show that they do. A similar question about רבי שמעון is answered from the חכמים of the משנה: one tribe that followed the בית דין הגדול does bring a קרבן. The גמרא then looks for the source that one tribe is called a קהל, and settles on the promise to יעקב before בנימין was born. Finally it begins a ברייתא of רבי שמעון about the חטאת of the לוים, which is compared to the עולה and not eaten. That teaching continues on the next amud.

steps.title: What is the source for 'ruling by the court, action by the people'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where רבי שמעון and רבי מאיר learn that the ruling depends on the בית דין and the action depends on the קהל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי שמעון and רבי מאיר, who hold that the ruling depends on the court and the action depends on the congregation: where do they learn this from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of an idea that רבי שמעון and רבי מאיר share. This question sets up the next two answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both of these תנאים agree that a communal offering requires two things: a mistaken ruling from the בית דין and a sin done by the people. The גמרא wants a פסוק showing that both elements are needed.

keyTerms.meaning: A halachic ruling issued by the court
The actual action (the sin that was done)
From where do they know it?

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon and Rabbi Meir,
who hold that the ruling depends on the court
and the action depends on the congregation,
from where do they learn this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion of the משנה's opinions
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A פסוק that shows the ruling comes from the court and the action comes from the people

steps.title: אביי's source: 'from the eyes of the congregation'
steps.stepSummary: אביי brings the פסוק ״והיה אם מעיני העדה נעשתה לשגגה״.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: the פסוק says, 'And it shall be, if from the eyes of the congregation it was done unwittingly.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question with a פסוק from במדבר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks of something hidden 'from the eyes of the עדה' (the court), while the sin itself 'was done'. That shows the court's ruling caused the people's action, so the ruling and the action are two separate parts.

keyTerms.meaning: From the eyes of the congregation (here meaning the court)

phrases.english: Abaye said,
for the verse says:
"And it shall be, if from the eyes of the congregation
it was done unwittingly."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is ״מעיני העדה נעשתה לשגגה״: the court's eyes went wrong, and the people did the action

steps.title: רבא's source: 'for all the people unwittingly'
steps.stepSummary: רבא brings a different פסוק: ״לכל העם בשגגה״.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: it is learned from 'for all the people it was unwittingly.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא offers a second answer from a later פסוק in the same section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'all the people' show that the mistake belongs to everyone together: the court through its ruling and the people through their action.

phrases.english: Rava said:
From "for all the people it was unwittingly."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second source as an alternative to אביי

steps.title: Why both פסוקים are needed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that each פסוק teaches something the other would leave out.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both are needed. If the Torah had written only 'from the eyes of the congregation,' I would have said that even a minority sinning is enough, so it wrote 'all the people.' If it had written only 'all the people,' I would have said there is no obligation until the court itself sins together with the majority, so it wrote 'from the eyes of the congregation.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the two פסוקים do not repeat each other. Each one blocks a mistake we might make with only the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'From the eyes of the congregation' teaches that the court's ruling causes the sin, but alone it might allow even a minority of the people. 'All the people' requires a majority, but alone it might seem to require the court to sin together with the people. Together they teach that the court rules and the majority acts.

keyTerms.meaning: And it is necessary (both sources are needed)
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah

steps.confusionAlert: Here the גמרא combines אביי's פסוק and רבא's פסוק. Do not read this as a separate argument between them; the point is that both פסוקים are needed for the full law.

phrases.english: And both are necessary,
for if the Merciful One had written only
"And it shall be, if from the eyes of the congregation
it was done unwittingly,"
I would have said: even a minority is enough,
therefore it is written "for all the people unwittingly."
And if it had written only "for all the people unwittingly,"

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה אָמֵינָא: עַד דְּעָבְדִי בֵּית דִּין בַּהֲדֵי רוּבָּא,
phrases.english: I would have said: not until the court acts together with the majority,
therefore it is written
"And it shall be, if from the eyes of the congregation it was done unwittingly."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the sources of both אביי and רבא are needed
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A communal offering requires a ruling by the court plus an action by a majority of the people; the court does not need to act itself

steps.title: These פסוקים are about idol worship
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that these פסוקים are written about עבודה זרה, not other sins.
steps.simpleTranslation: But when these פסוקים are written, they are written about idol worship!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the sources just brought. How can פסוקים about עבודה זרה teach the rule for other sins?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The section in במדבר 15 deals with a communal mistake in עבודה זרה. The law of the communal offering for other sins appears elsewhere, so the proof seems to be from the wrong topic.

phrases.english: But when these verses are written,
it is about idol worship that they are written.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the sources from steps 2 to 4
steps.kashyaTarget: Using the פסוקים in במדבר 15 as a source for all sins
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Those פסוקים are about עבודה זרה only, so they cannot teach the general law

steps.title: A גזרה שוה: 'from the eyes' and 'from the eyes'
steps.stepSummary: The word מעיני appears in both sections, so the rule carries over from עבודה זרה to other sins.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learn 'from the eyes' from 'from the eyes.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a word shared by both sections links them, so the law transfers from one to the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The section about other sins also says the matter was hidden 'מעיני הקהל'. Because the same word מעיני appears in both places, whatever is learned about עבודה זרה applies to other sins as well.

keyTerms.meaning: From the eyes of: the shared word linking the two sections

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי מאיר and רבי שמעון, the ruling comes from the court and the action from the majority of the people. This is learned from two פסוקים about עבודה זרה and extended to all sins through the shared word מעיני.

phrases.english: We derive it from "from the eyes" and "from the eyes."
phrases.notes: The section about other sins also says "מעיני הקהל" (ויקרא 4:13), so the two sections are linked.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 5
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוקים apply only to עבודה זרה
steps.terutzMaskana: Through the shared word מעיני, the law applies to other sins too

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about one tribe's court
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה: 'If the court of one tribe ruled, etc.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'If the court of one tribe issued a ruling, etc.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new section by quoting a line from the משנה. This sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי יהודה holds that when a tribe's own court ruled and that tribe sinned, only that tribe brings an offering. The גמרא will now ask about a related case.

keyTerms.meaning: Etc.: the rest of the משנה line

phrases.aramaic: הוֹרוּ בֵּית דִּין שֶׁל אֶחָד וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: "If the court of one [tribe] issued a ruling, etc."

steps.triggerLanguage: הוֹרוּ בֵּית דִּין שֶׁל אֶחָד וְכוּ׳
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In רבי יהודה's view, a tribe that sinned by its own court's ruling brings an offering, and the other tribes are exempt

steps.title: One tribe sinned by the בית דין הגדול's ruling: do the others bring?
steps.stepSummary: A question is raised in רבי יהודה's view: if one tribe sinned because of a ruling by the בית דין הגדול, do the other tribes bring offerings?
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: according to רבי יהודה, if one tribe sinned because of a ruling of the Great Court, do the other tribes bring an offering or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises an open question (an איבעיא) about a case the משנה does not address directly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's case was a tribe following its own court. Here the ruling came from the בית דין הגדול, which serves all of Israel, but only one tribe acted on it. The question is whether the other tribes are pulled in.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before them

phrases.english: It was asked of them:
One tribe, according to Rabbi Yehuda,
that acted on a ruling of the Great Court,

phrases.aramaic: מִי מַיְיתוּ שְׁאָר שְׁבָטִים אוֹ לָא?
phrases.english: do the other tribes bring an offering or not?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a case that grows out of the משנה just quoted
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the other tribes bring an offering when one tribe sinned by a ruling of the בית דין הגדול

steps.title: The two sides of the question
steps.stepSummary: Maybe the other tribes join only when seven tribes, a majority, sinned. Or maybe the number makes no difference.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we say that only when seven tribes sinned do the other tribes bring with them, because there is a majority, but with one tribe, where there is no majority, they do not? Or perhaps there is no difference!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lays out the two possible ways to answer the question. It does not decide yet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי יהודה's view, when seven tribes sin, the remaining tribes also bring offerings along with them. One side says this happens only because seven is a majority; the other says the other tribes are drawn in even by one tribe.

phrases.english: Do we say:
it is only with seven tribes that they bring,
phrases.notes: In the משנה, רבי יהודה says that when seven tribes sin, the other tribes bring offerings along with them.

phrases.english: meaning the other tribes bring together with them,
because there is a majority,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל חַד שֵׁבֶט, דְּלֵיכָּא רוּבָּא – לָא,
phrases.english: but with one tribe, where there is no majority, they do not,
or perhaps there is no difference!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the two sides of the question in step 8
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the other tribes join only because of a majority, or even after just one tribe

steps.title: A first proof from a ברייתא: one bull or two bulls
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא (תנא קמא: one bull; רבי שמעון: two bulls) and shows that the case must be one tribe sinning by a ruling of the בית דין הגדול.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: What do they bring? One bull. רבי שמעון says: Two bulls. What case is this? If seven tribes sinned, רבי שמעון would require eight bulls! So it must be that one tribe sinned. Based on what ruling? If it followed its own tribal court, רבי שמעון does not accept that idea at all! So it must be a ruling of the בית דין הגדול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins trying to answer its question from Steps 8-9 with a ברייתא. First it works out exactly which case the ברייתא is talking about, using רבי שמעון's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון holds that each tribe that sinned brings its own bull, and the court brings one more. So 'two bulls' cannot mean seven tribes sinned, since that would be eight bulls. It must mean one tribe plus the court. And since רבי שמעון does not accept liability from a tribal court's ruling, the ruling must have come from the בית דין הגדול.

keyTerms.meaning: A bull brought as an offering for a communal mistake
What case are we dealing with?
He does not hold of it, he does not accept this idea

phrases.english: Come and hear:
What do they bring? One bull.
Rabbi Shimon says: Two bulls.
What case are we dealing with?
If you say that seven [tribes] sinned,
Rabbi Shimon would require eight!
phrases.notes: Seven bulls for the seven tribes, plus one for the court.

phrases.english: Rather, it is where one tribe sinned.
Based on what [ruling]?
If it was based on a ruling of its own [tribal] court,
Rabbi Shimon does not accept that!

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לָאו בְּהוֹרָאַת בֵּית דִּין הַגָּדוֹל.
phrases.english: Rather, is it not based on a ruling of the High Court?

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: מָה הֵן מְבִיאִין? פַּר אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts trying to answer the question raised in Steps 8-9.
steps.raayaObject: Whether other tribes bring offerings when one tribe sinned by a ruling of the בית דין הגדול, in רבי יהודה's view.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about how many bulls are brought (תנא קמא: one; רבי שמעון: two).

steps.title: The first opinion must be רבי יהודה, so only one bull is brought
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא cannot be רבי מאיר, who requires a majority, so it must be רבי יהודה, who says only one bull when one tribe sinned.
steps.simpleTranslation: And who is the first תנא? If you say רבי מאיר, he requires a majority! So it must be רבי יהודה, in a case where one tribe sinned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof by figuring out who the first opinion in the ברייתא is. It concludes that it is רבי יהודה, talking about one tribe that sinned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר says no bull is brought unless a majority sinned, so he could not be talking about one tribe. That leaves רבי יהודה, and he says only 'one bull.' This seems to show that when one tribe sinned, even by a ruling of the High Court, the other tribes do not join and bring bulls.

keyTerms.meaning: The first opinion in a משנה or ברייתא, said without a name

phrases.english: And who is the first tanna?
If you say it is Rabbi Meir,
But he requires a majority!
Rather, is it not Rabbi Yehuda,
and the case is where one tribe sinned?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof begun in Step 10 by identifying the first opinion.
steps.raayaObject: That in רבי יהודה's view, the other tribes do not bring offerings when one tribe sinned.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The תנא קמא's ruling of 'one bull' in the ברייתא, read as רבי יהודה.

steps.title: Rejecting the proof: the case may be six tribes who are a majority
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes away the proof: the ברייתא may be about six tribes that are most of the people, and follow רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: What case is this? Six tribes sinned, and they are most of the people, and it follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. As a ברייתא teaches: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says in his name: If six tribes sinned and they are most of the people, or seven tribes sinned even though they are not most of the people, a bull is brought.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from Steps 10-11. It says the ברייתא might be talking about a different case, so it says nothing about one tribe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof assumed the first opinion had to be רבי יהודה with one tribe. But it could be רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, who quotes רבי מאיר: six tribes that are most of the population count as a majority. Then 'one bull' fits a majority case, and the proof about one tribe falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: Most of the people (by number of people)

steps.confusionAlert: There are two kinds of majority here: most of the tribes (seven out of twelve), or most of the people (six tribes that have more than half the population). Either one is enough for רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.

phrases.english: They say: What case are we dealing with here?
A case where six tribes sinned
and they are the majority of the people,
and it follows Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar.

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר מִשְּׁמוֹ:
phrases.english: As it was taught: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says in his name:
phrases.notes: 'In his name' means in the name of רבי מאיר.

phrases.aramaic: חָטְאוּ שִׁשָּׁה וְהֵן רוּבּוֹ שֶׁל קָהָל,
phrases.english: If six sinned and they are the majority of the people,
or seven [sinned],

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינָן רוּבּוֹ שֶׁל קָהָל –
phrases.english: even though they are not the majority of the people,
they bring a bull.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof built in Steps 10-11.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from the ברייתא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It wrongly assumed the first opinion must be רבי יהודה talking about one tribe; it could be רבי שמעון בן אלעזר talking about six tribes that are a majority of the people.

steps.title: A clear ברייתא in רבי יהודה's name
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי יהודה directly: a tribal court ruling makes only that tribe liable, but a ruling of the בית דין הגדול makes even the other tribes liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי יהודה says: A tribe that acted on a ruling of its own court, that tribe is liable and all the other tribes are exempt. But with a ruling of the בית דין הגדול, even the other tribes are liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second source, this time with רבי יהודה's own words, which speaks directly to the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה makes a contrast. If only a tribal court ruled, only that tribe brings an offering. But if the בית דין הגדול ruled and one tribe acted on it, the other tribes are liable too, even though they did not sin.

keyTerms.meaning: Its own court: the tribe's local court
The High Court, the great סנהדרין
Exempt, do not bring an offering

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that in רבי יהודה's view, a ruling of the בית דין הגדול ties all of כלל ישראל together, so one tribe's mistake involves everyone.

phrases.english: Come and hear: Rabbi Yehuda says:
A tribe that acted on a ruling of its own court,
that tribe is liable,
and all the other tribes are exempt.
But on a ruling of the High Court,
even the other tribes are liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof was rejected in Step 12, brings a new and clearer source.
steps.raayaObject: That in רבי יהודה's view, the other tribes bring offerings when one tribe sinned by a ruling of the בית דין הגדול.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא quoting רבי יהודה directly.

steps.title: Conclusion: the other tribes are liable too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes from the ברייתא that, according to רבי יהודה, the other tribes bring offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא declares that the question from Steps 8-9 is answered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא in Step 13 talks about one tribe that acted on a ruling of the בית דין הגדול, and says the other tribes are liable. So the number of tribes that sinned does not matter, and the other tribes join even when only one tribe sinned.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it: the question is settled

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יהודה: a tribal court's ruling makes only the sinning tribe liable, but a ruling of the בית דין הגדול makes all the tribes liable, even when only one tribe sinned.

phrases.english: Learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the final answer from the ברייתא in Step 13.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In רבי יהודה's view, when even one tribe sins by a ruling of the בית דין הגדול, the other tribes also bring offerings; the number of sinning tribes makes no difference.

steps.title: רב אשי brings support from the wording of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says the משנה's own wording supports the conclusion about רבי יהודה, and quotes the line he will analyze.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: The משנה is also precise this way. It says: 'That tribe acted on their ruling. That tribe is liable, and all the other tribes are exempt.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי adds a second proof for the conclusion of step 14, this time from the משנה itself. He quotes the line first, and the next steps will show why its wording matters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 proved רבי יהודה's view from a ברייתא. רב אשי says our משנה hints at the same idea. The key words are 'and all the other tribes are exempt.'

keyTerms.meaning: is precise; its exact wording shows something
liable; obligated to bring an offering

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
The Mishnah is also precise [this way],
phrases.notes: He means the wording of our משנה also supports what we just concluded about רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: for it teaches:
"And that tribe acted according to their ruling —
phrases.notes: 'Their ruling' is the ruling of that tribe's own court.

phrases.english: that tribe is liable
and all the rest of the tribes are exempt."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, independent support for the conclusion of step 14.
steps.raayaObject: That by רבי יהודה, other tribes are liable when one tribe sins by a ruling of the בית דין הגדול.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The wording of our משנה: 'that tribe is liable and all the other tribes are exempt.'

steps.title: Why does the משנה need to say the other tribes are exempt?
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי points out that 'the other tribes are exempt' seems extra, since it follows from 'that tribe is liable.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Why does the משנה need to say 'the other tribes are exempt'? It already said 'that tribe is liable.' Once it said that, I would know by myself that the other tribes are exempt!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי notices that the משנה seems to say something obvious. He is setting up his proof: if the words seem extra, they must be there to teach something.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If only 'that tribe' is liable, then clearly nobody else is. So the words 'the other tribes are exempt' look unneeded. The question opens the door to the answer in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: why do I need it? (asked about words that seem extra)

phrases.english: Why do I need [the Mishnah] to teach
"and the rest of the tribes are exempt"?
It already taught "that tribe is liable,"
and since it taught "that tribe is liable,"
I would automatically know
that the rest of the tribes are exempt!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the extra words in the משנה line just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What do the seemingly extra words 'the other tribes are exempt' come to teach?

steps.title: The extra words teach a difference between the two courts
steps.stepSummary: The extra words teach that the other tribes are exempt only when the tribe followed its own court. When it followed the בית דין הגדול, the other tribes are liable too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is what it teaches us: the other tribes are exempt only when the tribe followed its own court. But when it followed the בית דין הגדול, even the other tribes are liable.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers his own question. The extra words limit the exemption to a ruling of the tribe's own court.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'the other tribes are exempt' here hints that in a different case they are not exempt. That case is a ruling of the בית דין הגדול. This is exactly רבי יהודה's view from the ברייתא in step 13.

keyTerms.meaning: this is what it teaches us
a ruling of the tribe's own court

phrases.english: Rather, this is what it teaches us:
it is with a ruling of its own court
that the rest of the tribes are exempt,
but with a ruling of the Great Court —
even the rest of the tribes are liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16 by giving the extra words a purpose.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words limit the exemption to a ruling of the tribe's own court. With a ruling of the בית דין הגדול, the other tribes are liable.

steps.title: The proof from the משנה stands
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts רב אשי's reading of the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the proof. The משנה supports רבי יהודה's view that other tribes bring offerings in this case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This closes the line of steps 8–17. Both a ברייתא and the wording of the משנה show that by רבי יהודה, a ruling of the בית דין הגדול makes even the other tribes liable.

keyTerms.meaning: learn from it; the proof is accepted

steps.whatToRemember: By רבי יהודה: if one tribe sins because of its own court, only that tribe brings an offering. If it sins because of the בית דין הגדול, the other tribes bring offerings too.

phrases.english: Learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the proof of steps 15–17.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה supports רבי יהודה: with a ruling of the בית דין הגדול, even the other tribes are liable.

steps.title: Does one tribe bring an offering according to רבי שמעון?
steps.stepSummary: A new question: by רבי שמעון, does one tribe that sinned because of the בית דין הגדול bring an offering?
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: if one tribe acted on a ruling of the בית דין הגדול, does it bring an offering according to רבי שמעון, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question, now about רבי שמעון instead of רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already know רבי שמעון does not make a tribe liable for its own court's ruling. The question is whether he does make one tribe liable when the ruling came from the בית דין הגדול.

keyTerms.meaning: a question was asked of them (the Sages)

phrases.english: A question was asked of them:
One tribe that acted
by a ruling of the Great Court,

phrases.aramaic: לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מִי מַיְיתֵי אוֹ לָא?
phrases.english: according to Rabbi Shimon, do they bring [an offering] or not?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from רבי יהודה's view to a new question about רבי שמעון.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: By רבי שמעון, is one tribe that sinned by a ruling of the בית דין הגדול obligated to bring an offering?

steps.title: A proof from the one-bull and two-bulls ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries to prove from the ברייתא of 'one bull / two bulls' that by רבי שמעון, one tribe does bring an offering after a ruling of the בית דין הגדול.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: What do they bring? One bull. רבי שמעון says: two bulls. Which case is this? If seven tribes sinned, would רבי שמעון say only two bulls? He would need eight! So it must be one tribe that sinned. Because of whose ruling? If its own court, רבי שמעון does not accept that. So it must be a ruling of the בית דין הגדול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the ברייתא from step 10 to answer the new question. It narrows down the case until only one option is left: one tribe that followed the בית דין הגדול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It cannot be seven tribes, because רבי שמעון would then need eight bulls, not two. It cannot be a tribe following its own court, because רבי שמעון does not hold of that. So רבי שמעון's 'two bulls' must mean one tribe that followed the בית דין הגדול does bring.

keyTerms.meaning: what case are we dealing with?
he does not hold of it

phrases.english: Come and hear:
What do they bring? One bull;
Rabbi Shimon says: two bulls.
What case are we dealing with?
If you say that seven [tribes] sinned —
two bulls?
Eight bulls are needed!
phrases.notes: By רבי שמעון, each of the seven tribes brings its own bull, plus one more for the court.

phrases.english: Rather, one tribe sinned,
and through what [ruling]?
If you say by a ruling of its own court,
Rabbi Shimon doesn't hold of that!
Rather, by a ruling of the Great Court.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: מָה הֵן מְבִיאִין? פַּר אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer the question of step 19 using the ברייתא first brought in step 10.
steps.raayaObject: That by רבי שמעון, one tribe that sinned by a ruling of the בית דין הגדול brings an offering.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא: 'one bull; רבי שמעון says two bulls,' read as a case of one tribe.

steps.title: The תנא קמא must be רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, so the proof fails
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. Neither רבי מאיר nor רבי יהודה fits the תנא קמא, so it must be רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, and the case is six large tribes, not one tribe.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can you really think so? Then who is the תנא קמא? If רבי מאיר, he requires a majority. If רבי יהודה, the other tribes would also bring. Rather, it is רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, as taught in the ברייתא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof of step 20 by asking who the תנא קמא could be. Only רבי שמעון בן אלעזר fits, and in his case more than one tribe sinned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר needs a majority of the people to sin, so one tribe is not enough for him. רבי יהודה would have the other tribes bring too, so there would be more than one bull. The ברייתא therefore follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר: six tribes that are most of the people sinned. So it tells us nothing about one tribe according to רבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: and can you really think so? (opens a rejection)
the first, unnamed opinion in a teaching

steps.confusionAlert: In step 11 the גמרא said the תנא קמא was רבי יהודה. Now that we know רבי יהודה has the other tribes bring too, he no longer fits, so the תנא קמא must be רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
steps.whatToRemember: This proof fails: the 'one bull / two bulls' ברייתא is about six tribes that are most of the people, following רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, so it says nothing about one tribe. The question about רבי שמעון is answered in steps 22–23.

phrases.english: And can you really think so?
Who is the first Tanna?

phrases.aramaic: אִי רַבִּי מֵאִיר – הָא רוּבָּא בָּעֵי,
phrases.english: If Rabbi Meir — he requires a majority,
if Rabbi Yehuda —
the rest of the tribes also bring!
phrases.notes: We just learned this in steps 14–18, so for רבי יהודה it wouldn't be only one bull.

phrases.english: Rather, whose view is this?
It is Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar,
and as it was taught [in a Baraita].
phrases.notes: This points back to the ברייתא about six tribes that are most of the people.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 20 by redefining the case of the ברייתא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the whole proof from the ברייתא for רבי שמעון's view about one tribe.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the case was one tribe. But the תנא קמא can only be רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, whose case is six tribes that are most of the people.

steps.title: Proof from the words of the חכמים in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the חכמים of the משנה, who say one is liable only for a ruling of the בית דין הגדול. It shows that these חכמים cannot be רבי מאיר, so they must be רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'And the חכמים say: one is never liable except for a ruling of the בית דין הגדול.' Who are these חכמים? If you say רבי מאיר, he requires a majority! So is it not רבי שמעון?
steps.whatsHappening: After the last proof failed, the גמרא tries again to answer the question from step 19. It uses the opinion of the חכמים in our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים are talking about one tribe that sinned, and they say it is liable when it followed the בית דין הגדול. רבי מאיר cannot be the author, because he says there is no קרבן unless a majority sinned. So the חכמים must be רבי שמעון, which means that by רבי שמעון one tribe does bring a קרבן after a ruling of the בית דין הגדול.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, the unnamed opinion in the משנה
If you say (the first option, which will be rejected)

steps.confusionAlert: Here the word חכמים does not mean 'the majority of Sages.' The גמרא is asking which specific named תנא stands behind the anonymous label.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
And the Sages say:
One is never liable

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא עַל הוֹרָאַת בֵּית דִּין הַגָּדוֹל.
phrases.english: except for a ruling of the High Court.
Who are the Sages?
If you say Rabbi Meir,
he requires a majority!
phrases.notes: For רבי מאיר, one tribe alone could never bring a קרבן, so he can't be the one speaking here.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not Rabbi Shimon?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new attempt to answer the question of step 19, after the proof in step 20 was rejected in step 21.
steps.raayaObject: That by רבי שמעון one tribe that followed the בית דין הגדול brings a קרבן.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The statement of the חכמים in the משנה, identified as רבי שמעון by ruling out רבי מאיר.

steps.title: The proof is accepted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts the proof: by רבי שמעון, one tribe that followed the בית דין הגדול is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the proof from step 22 and closes the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the חכמים must be רבי שמעון, the question of step 19 is now answered. By רבי שמעון, one tribe does bring a קרבן when it followed the בית דין הגדול.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it: the proof is accepted

steps.whatToRemember: By רבי שמעון, one tribe that sinned by following the בית דין הגדול brings a קרבן. The proof comes from the חכמים of the משנה.

phrases.english: Conclude from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the proof of step 22.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: By רבי שמעון, one tribe that followed the בית דין הגדול is liable to bring a קרבן.

steps.title: Where do we learn that one tribe is called a קהל?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון use to show that a single tribe is called a קהל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון: from where do they learn that one tribe is called a קהל?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic. It asks for the source behind the idea that one tribe counts as a קהל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון hold that one tribe can bring a קרבן. The קרבן is for a קהל, so they need a source showing that one tribe alone is called a קהל.

keyTerms.meaning: A congregation: the group that brings the communal קרבן
From where do they know it?

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon,
that one tribe is called a congregation,
from where do they know it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, שֵׁבֶט אֶחָד דְּאִקְּרִי קָהָל מְנָא לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about the source for the opinions of רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק showing that a single tribe is called a קהל.

steps.title: First source: יהושפט in the קהל of יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The answer is a פסוק where יהושפט stands 'in the קהל of יהודה and ירושלים', so the tribe of יהודה is called a קהל.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: as it is written, 'And יהושפט stood in the קהל of יהודה and ירושלים, in the house of ה׳, before the new courtyard.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a first source: a פסוק that uses the word קהל for the tribe of יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק calls the people of יהודה a קהל. That suggests a single tribe can be called a קהל.

phrases.english: They say: as it is written:
"And Jehoshaphat stood
in the congregation of Judah and Jerusalem
(opposite the courtyard of the house of the Lord)
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the words in round brackets. The words in square brackets are the corrected wording, matching the פסוק.

phrases.english: [in the house of the Lord, before the courtyard]
that was new."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'בקהל יהודה וירושלים' calls the tribe of יהודה a קהל.

steps.title: What is the 'new' courtyard?
steps.stepSummary: A side question about the פסוק just quoted: what does the word 'new' mean?
steps.simpleTranslation: What is 'new'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to explain a word in the פסוק it just quoted. This sets up רבי יוחנן's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The courtyard was not newly built, so the word 'new' needs an explanation. This is a side point and does not change the proof about קהל.

phrases.english: What is "new"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side question on a word in the פסוק of step 25.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the word 'חדשה' in the פסוק.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: they made a new rule
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that 'new' means they made a new rule then: a טבול יום may not enter the מחנה לויה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: they made new rules and said that a טבול יום may not enter the מחנה לויה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the side question. The courtyard was called 'new' because of a new rule made at that time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The courtyard itself was not new. What was new was a rabbinic rule that someone who immersed today and is waiting for nightfall may not even enter the מחנה לויה.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone who immersed today and is waiting for nightfall to be fully pure
The Levite camp: the area of הר הבית

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
That they made new matters and said:
One who immersed that day
may not enter the Levite camp.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the side question of step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'New' means a new rule was made: a טבול יום may not enter the מחנה לויה.

steps.title: רב אחא בר יעקב: ירושלים also belonged to בנימין
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב attacks the proof: ירושלים was partly in בנימין, so the פסוק speaks of two tribes, not one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב challenged it: From where do you know? Maybe ירושלים is different, because it was also part of בנימין!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the main proof from step 25 and challenges it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'יהודה and ירושלים.' Since ירושלים was partly in בנימין's land, the קהל in the פסוק may include two tribes. That proves nothing about one tribe alone.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב:
phrases.english: Rav Aḥa bar Ya'akov objected to it:
From where do you know?
Perhaps Jerusalem is different,
since it was also Benjamin!
phrases.notes: He means part of ירושלים was in בנימין's land, so the קהל there was really two tribes.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the proof of step 25 and attacks it.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ירושלים belonged partly to בנימין, so the פסוק may describe two tribes together as a קהל, not one.

steps.title: New source: the promise to יעקב before בנימין's birth
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב brings a different פסוק: 'I will make you a קהל of peoples.' The only son born after that was בנימין, so one tribe is called a קהל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב אחא בר יעקב said: as it is written, 'And He said to me: I will make you fruitful and multiply you, and make you a קהל of peoples.' Who was born to him after that time? בנימין. Learn from it that this is what the תורה is saying: another קהל will now be born to you.
steps.whatsHappening: Having rejected the first source, רב אחא בר יעקב gives a new source to answer the question of step 24.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ה׳ promised יעקב a new 'קהל', and the only son born after that promise was בנימין. So בנימין, one tribe, is the 'קהל' being promised. This shows that a single tribe is called a קהל.

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One: ה׳, or the Torah

steps.whatToRemember: The accepted source that one tribe is a קהל is 'ונתתיך לקהל עמים', said to יעקב when only בנימין was still to be born.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב,
phrases.english: Rather, Rav Aḥa bar Ya'akov said:
As it is written: "And He said to me:
phrases.notes: בראשית 48:4. יעקב is telling יוסף what ה׳ said to him.

phrases.english: Behold, I will make you fruitful and multiply you,
and I will make you a congregation of peoples, etc."
Who was born to him after that time?
Benjamin.
Conclude from it that this is what the Merciful One is saying:
Another congregation will now be born to you.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the source rejected in step 28 with a new one.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: From 'ונתתיך לקהל עמים': the only son still to be born was בנימין, so one tribe is called a קהל.

steps.title: רב שבא: maybe the קהל means all twelve tribes
steps.stepSummary: רב שבא suggests the promise means that once בנימין is born, all twelve tribes together will be called a קהל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שבא said to רב כהנא: Maybe this is what the תורה is telling him: once בנימין is born to you, then there will be twelve tribes, and they are what is called a קהל!
steps.whatsHappening: רב שבא challenges the new proof from step 29.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads the פסוק differently. The 'קהל' is not בנימין alone, but the full group of twelve tribes that is completed when בנימין is born. If so, the פסוק says nothing about one tribe.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב שַׁבָּא לְרַב כָּהֲנָא,
phrases.english: Rav Shabba said to Rav Kahana:
Perhaps this is what the Merciful One is saying to him:
When Benjamin is born to you,
that is when there will be twelve tribes
which are called a congregation!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב שַׁבָּא לְרַב כָּהֲנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading of the פסוק in step 29.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that 'קהל' in the promise refers to בנימין alone.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The 'קהל' could be the complete set of twelve tribes formed by בנימין's birth, not one tribe.

steps.title: רב כהנא: eleven tribes are surely a קהל too
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא answers that it makes no sense to say only twelve tribes are a קהל and eleven are not, so the new 'קהל' must be בנימין himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: So twelve tribes are called a קהל, and eleven tribes are not called a קהל?
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא defends the proof by showing that רב שבא's reading does not make sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יעקב already had eleven tribes, and they were surely already a קהל. So the promise of a new קהל cannot mean the completed twelve. It must mean בנימין alone, which proves that one tribe is called a קהל.
steps.whatToRemember: The proof from 'לקהל עמים' stands: since eleven tribes were already a קהל, the new קהל promised is בנימין alone. So a single tribe is a קהל, which supports רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון.

phrases.english: He said to him:

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר שְׁבָטִים אִיקְּרוּ קָהָל,
phrases.english: But then, twelve tribes are called a congregation,

phrases.aramaic: אַחַד עָשָׂר שְׁבָטִים לֹא אִיקְּרוּ קָהָל?
phrases.english: and eleven tribes are not called a congregation?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֶלָּא שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר שְׁבָטִים אִיקְּרוּ קָהָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב שבא's challenge in step 30 and keeps the proof of step 29 standing.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rhetorical question showing the challenger's reading makes no sense.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The 'קהל' in the promise could be the full twelve tribes.
steps.terutzMaskana: Eleven tribes were already a קהל, so the new קהל promised must be בנימין alone. One tribe is called a קהל.

steps.title: Why does the פסוק say 'a second bull'?
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון asks what the words 'and a second bull' add, since another פסוק already says there were two bulls, one a חטאת and one an עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: רבי שמעון says, why does the פסוק say 'And a second young bull you shall take for a חטאת'? If it is to teach that there are two bulls, another פסוק already says, 'Make the one a חטאת and the other an עולה to ה''!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא where רבי שמעון points out that a word in the פסוק seems extra. This sets up his answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'second' looks like it only tells us there were two bulls. But במדבר 8:12 already says 'the one... and the other', so we know there were two. Since the תורה has no extra words, 'second' must teach something new.

keyTerms.meaning: Why does the פסוק need to say this? (a sign that a word looks extra)
Burnt-offering, burned completely on the מזבח

steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does the word 'second' in במדבר 8:8 teach, since there being two bulls is already known from במדבר 8:12?

steps.title: 'Second' ties the חטאת to the עולה, so it is not eaten
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון answers that 'second' compares the חטאת to the עולה: just as the עולה is not eaten, so too the חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, you might think the חטאת brought for the לוים is eaten. So the פסוק says 'and a second bull', meaning second to the עולה. Just as the עולה is not eaten...
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון answers his own question: the word 'second' teaches that this חטאת is treated like the עולה. The sentence is cut off here and continues next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the כהנים eat the meat of a חטאת. 'Second' links this חטאת to the עולה mentioned with it. Since an עולה is fully burned and never eaten, this חטאת is not eaten either.

keyTerms.meaning: One might have thought (a wrong idea the פסוק comes to rule out)
The לוים, the tribe of לוי
Second to the עולה, so it is compared to the עולה

steps.confusionAlert: 'Second' does not mean 'one more bull' here. רבי שמעון reads it as 'next to the עולה and like it', which is why the חטאת is not eaten.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the חטאת brought for the לוים had a special rule, different from a regular חטאת.
